user.title: ClimateML
user.description: Add the ClimateML integration. Configure global settings in Options; add zones and configure the controller via the integration page after setup.

abort.single_instance_allowed: Only one ClimateML instance is allowed

data_description.name: Display name — used to generate the stable zone ID
data_description.head_entity: The climate entity controlling this zone's heat pump head
data_description.sensor_entity: The sensor reporting actual room temperature
data_description.eva_in_entity: Refrigerant inlet temperature from ESPHome samsung-hvac — logged for future ML
data_description.eva_out_entity: Refrigerant outlet temperature from ESPHome samsung-hvac — logged for future ML
data_description.weekday_blocks: Time blocks for Monday–Friday. Add as many as needed.
data_description.weekend_blocks: Time blocks for Saturday–Sunday. Add as many as needed.

data_description.eva_in_entity: Refrigerant inlet temperature from ESPHome samsung-hvac
data_description.eva_out_entity: Refrigerant outlet temperature from ESPHome samsung-hvac

data_description.odu_mode_entity: Compressor/ODU operating mode — ground truth for heat pump state (e.g. sensor.samsung_hvac_odu_mode)
data_description.outdoor_temp_entity: Outdoor temperature — used as additional peer reading for sensor guard
data_description.extra_temp_entities: Non-zone indoor sensors (e.g. hallway) used as peer readings in the sensor guard anomaly check
data_description.power_entity: Real-time power draw — logged for future COP calculations
data_description.energy_entity: Cumulative energy — logged for future efficiency trending
data_description.weather_entity: Used to fetch hourly forecast for solar gain anticipation (future ML feature)

data_description.update_interval_minutes: How often the decision loop runs
data_description.hallway_sensor: Used as a whole-house reference temperature
data_description.outdoor_sensor: Legacy outdoor sensor — prefer ODU outdoor entity in Controller
